title: Lollipop Jones, Red Fox and the Dewdrop comedians; dating his early years
summary: Longhair recalls the comedian Lollipop Jones; the interviewer notes comedians at the Dewdrop; they date the minstrel show to about 1925 and tap dancing to the early 1930s.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well, lollipops. I don't know whether you heard of him. Lollipop. Yeah, lollipop Jones. Lollipop Jones in Memphis. Memphis, uh, Lewis. Lewis. Memphis Lewis.

Oh, you know some shit. Oh man, I told you, I could come into these things, you gotta know some things, you know? You know, just, uh, come in here and scare them, you know? I know, but I've been in a while to interviews with him and you know some shit nobody else knows. I know, you don't think I'm gonna come in here half-cum.
I'm already light. Okay, so when you meet, now Lollipop was a great comedian. He was. You must have learned a lot from him. He was. He was great. I mean, I know I've seen, I know.

At the Dewdrop. Yeah, I'll bet Red Fox did. All those comedians came to the Dewdrop.
Yeah, a pleasure work with him.

All those comedians came, I'll bet. Yeah. All the great comedians of the 50s, black comedians, all came to the Dewdrop. You know Scoey Mitchell? Scoey Mitchell used to work at the Dewdrop. Yeah, oh yeah, way before I was a small kid.
What year was this when you said you went with the Minstrel Show? Oh, I was small.
I was around seven, eight years old, delivering papers and shining shoes and running on the air.
So this must have been 19, about 1925 or so?
Somewhere around there, 25, 26, somewhere down there.
And then when you started tap dancing with, uh... I was around about 13, 14 years old. That could have been more, about 1932 or so, sometime in there. Had to be.
